# T-102 P1 / PR3 plan review

Date: October 17, 2026.

**Verdict: approve the bounded compatibility-spike proposal.** No blocking
finding for that scope. The three pre-spike owner questions have explicit
recorded resolutions. Current reviewer policy permits this separate reviewer
session. This verdict is independent plan review, not final owner acceptance,
implementation acceptance, task promotion, dispatch, or permission to run a
probe in this session.

## Findings, ordered by severity

### Medium, nonblocking successor-plan requirement: mutation safety comes first

P1:511-543 proposes mutable task capture and handoff in slice 2, while
P1:546-582 assigns durable recovery and duplicate-mutation acceptance to
slice 3. The shared contracts already require durable request receipts and
exact owner-action binding (P1:380-409,411-461), but the later decomposition
must put those prerequisites before the first production mutation.

Carry forward the pinned T-113 R2 Astra finding: either include durable
request/payload identity, mutation receipts, canonical pending decisions and
trusted exact-action confirmation in the first mutation-capable slice, or
keep the earlier slice read-only/fixture-only. Its acceptance must include a
lost acknowledgement after mutation, restart with a pending approval, and
reuse of a request ID with a conflicting payload. Include the selected durable
record paths in that slice's write scope. PR2's owner resolution explicitly
requires this ordering. It does not block a disposable compatibility probe;
none of the production slices is executable metadata in P1.

No blocking technical changes are requested to the submitted snapshot.

## Owner decisions and reviewer policy

Read the durable October 17 owner comments and the complete P1/PR2 decision
receipt. Each of P1's three exact frontmatter questions has a nonempty
`Resolved: <question> => <resolution>` entry in that receipt:

1. PM-first, extension-first, no-fork exploration is selected; preserve current
   defaults and exclude native workers. Reconcile T-109 before rollout.
2. Use the existing OpenAI subscription only through officially supported
   native sign-in. Discover and pin the supported Pi/runtime/model combination
   before live calls; stop if unsupported. At most five short compatibility
   calls, each at most 1024 output tokens, with $0 API spending. No paid API
   fallback or credential copying. Credentials and authentication remain in
   an isolated owner-controlled fixture, outside repository artifacts;
   actual sign-in is needed only if supported existing access is unavailable.
3. Only the bounded spike is selected. Establish its separate task/scope
   through normal workflow; production integration requires a successor
   independently reviewed plan and normal acceptance. No gate, identity,
   review, or future recovery requirement is waived.

The 20:48:38 UTC durable comment records the owner's delegation and bounded
defaults; PR2 at 20:50:50 UTC records their exact-question resolutions. PR2
escalated because independent technical approval was still required, not
because those three resolutions were absent. There is no unresolved
pre-spike owner choice requiring another escalation here. Support discovery
is a bounded investigation outcome, not an assumed entitlement. Insufficient
evidence within the five-call cap must remain unverified/no-go, not justify
extra calls or another provider route.

Transport/package/runtime acceptance after the spike, evaluation budget and
thresholds, a default switch, and native-worker scope remain later decisions.
They do not authorize action now. Final owner acceptance must still record
the applicable exact-question resolutions; this reviewer does not supply or
execute that owner verdict.

Current `corral route T-102 --json` resolves planner D4 and plan reviewer
`gpt-sol`, both `chatgpt-subscription/gpt-6.1-sol`, with
`require_cross_family: false` from the built-in default. PR3 is a separate
session, not a different-model review. This is permitted by
`docs/guide/plans.md:137-144` and
`crates/corral-ops/src/plan.rs:253-310`. The historical D4 `pending_reply`
same-profile/effective-model error is not a current policy mismatch.
PR3's recorded policy digest is
`2e109bee9d4c3b88db4d0f4cbc548d66ad5a6b02f7ef672098c16c55b82f93b5`.
No waiver or policy edit is needed or made.

## Scope, dependencies, and contracts

The goal and non-goals fit the proposal request: an owner-facing upstream Pi
conversation, Corral authority, a bundled first-party extension, unchanged
defaults, and retained OmO/omp workers. The plan separates reasoning/context
from orchestration and does not introduce a second authoritative database.

Only `pi-compatibility-contract-spike` is in frontmatter dependencies. Its
three write scopes are `docs/records/pi-native-compatibility.md`,
`docs/records/pi-native-protocol.md`, and `tools/pi-probe/`. It has no
dependencies and four observable acceptance scenarios, including a no-go
deliverable. The larger affected-path inventory describes later proposals,
not authorization to edit those production paths.

The proposed chain is spike -> bundled PM extension -> lifecycle/recovery ->
opt-in packaging/evaluation. Native workers/reviewers follow positive PM
evaluation and separate approval. Labels are unique, references resolve, and
both the executable graph and proposed graph are acyclic. Overlapping
production paths are ordered; the successor plan must confirm them after the
transport decision and apply the mutation-ordering requirement above.

At `crates/corral-ops/src/plan_decompose.rs:60-83`, zero/one-scope acceptance
attaches the plan and write scope to the original task; it does not create a
spike child or rewrite the proposal-only body. P1:119-134 correctly requires
separate task/scope establishment before dispatch. Do not implement directly
against this proposal-only parent. The historical Idea instruction versus
the existing planning/Review lifecycle is disclosed at P1:139-148; this review
does not move, queue, or dispatch the card.

The authority and transport contracts are appropriate:

- Shared Rust operations and canonical files retain task policy, admission,
  evidence, review and landing authority. Crate dependency directions remain
  compatible with `AGENTS.md` and `docs/DESIGN.md:59-65`.
- The native identity binds store/project/role/session generation and saved
  herdr socket/workspace/pane. Callback and mutation checks supplement the
  existing ownership contract (`docs/session-ownership.md:3-34`); peer UID,
  current config, or pane ID alone is insufficient.
- A private ownership-bound bridge must control the actual visible terminal
  conversation. Extension registration or a second hidden RPC session cannot
  substitute for that proof. Failure yields no-go, not terminal scraping.
- Acceptance, execution, pending obligations, provider/process failure,
  cancellation, settled turns and validated completion remain distinct facts.
  Legacy composer inspection in `crates/corral-herdr/src/delivery.rs:53-120` cannot
  become native-path evidence.
- Typed PM tools are bounded Rust operations, not arbitrary shell commands.
  Owner decisions use a trusted UI/board action bound to the exact action
  revision, not a model-selected actor or inferred approval.
- Durable PM obligations need an explicit container: existing
  `WaitRequest`/`DecisionRequest` require a run
  (`crates/corral-core/src/obligations.rs:26-49`), while the current PM remembers only
  a pane (`crates/corral-ops/src/pm.rs:9-12`). Runtime subscriptions, not model tools,
  perform asynchronous waits. Rotation gaps and ambiguous effects remain
  diagnosed uncertainty, not invented receipts.
- Packaging requires installed assets and exact support pins. Rollback uses
  canonical handoffs and retained tasks/questions/receipts, not transcript
  portability or credential conversion.

Current board readback confirms T-031/T-037/T-097/T-098/T-099/T-100 are Done
and T-048 is Dropped. T-109 and T-113 are now Done rather than their older
states in the snapshot. These are dated evidence updates, not a requirement
to revise immutable P1. A completed design/report still does not establish a
shipped lease API. Reinspect main and relevant reports before later work.

## Alternatives and risks

P1:655-665 compares retaining OmO, the recommended extension bridge, a thin
SDK host, RPC, generic CLI/MCP wrappers, Durable/fork/copied runtime, and
all-at-once native adoption. The recommended candidate preserves the required
terminal experience while explicitly reserving transport selection for a
measured spike. SDK/RPC alternatives must preserve that same conversation;
a new UI or hidden second conversation fails the stated goal.

The reviewed upstream moving documentation supports investigating those
primitives, not claiming a working native harness:

- [U1] `https://pi.dev/docs/latest/extensions`: session-scoped resources,
  final settlement, trusted same-user extension execution, and nested/deferred
  tool exposure. Hiding declarations is not sufficient permission enforcement.
- [U2] `https://pi.dev/docs/latest/sdk`: busy-input policy, subscriptions before
  prompting, listener rebinding after session replacement, resource/tool
  configuration.
- [U3] `https://pi.dev/docs/latest/rpc`: correlated responses are distinct from
  uncorrelated session events; accepted/queued/handled is not completion.
- [U4] `https://pi.dev/docs/latest/packages`: pinned sources, invocation-local
  loading, explicit resources, and host-provided peer dependencies.

These primary pages were read on October 17, 2026. Exact installed declarations
and runtime/package integrity remain spike deliverables. No subscription
compatibility, entitlement, cost saving, or model superiority is established.
T-031's mixed cost results concern OmO versus omp, not upstream Pi.

The risk table covers loss of useful OmO behavior, duplicate authority,
permission escape, lifecycle/restart/event loss, ambiguous effects, upstream
churn, provider access, premature rollout, and scope growth. Mitigations and
no-go/rollback routes are concrete. The 2-5-day spike and 2-4-week native-PM
allowances are explicitly estimates to revise, not measured promises.

## Acceptance and verification

The current task readback and durable task frontmatter have no registered
criterion manifest. No criterion IDs were invented. P1's seven existing
acceptance scenarios cover:

| Existing scenario | Plan-review result |
|---|---|
| Proposal rather than implementation | Pass: boundaries, alternatives, risks and staged approvals are explicit. |
| Separately authorized compatibility spike | Pass: single bounded executable scope; later work requires successor approval. |
| Clean-fixture native PM | Specified for later proof: normal launch, plain-language capture, real decision and mixed-harness result, with setup disclosed. |
| Busy delivery/restart/cancellation/ambiguous receipt | Specified: separate structured receipts, fencing, durable obligations and deduplication; retain the first-mutation prerequisite above. |
| Unauthorized transition or ended turn | Specified: Rust policy/ownership checks and validated completion remain mandatory. |
| Disable/upgrade/rollback | Specified: existing harnesses and canonical tasks, artifacts, questions and waits survive. |
| Default evaluation | Specified: frozen replay and matched live scenarios, coverage-aware spend, outcomes, rescues and a separate owner verdict. |

The deterministic matrix at P1:672-702 includes handled-without-run, busy
input, event gaps, pending questions, cancellation races, provider failure,
lost processes, duplicate/conflicting requests, stale/foreign callbacks,
permission bypass, unknown usage and rollback. Subscribe-before-trigger
synchronization, injected clocks and bounded deadlines avoid timing luck.
The real-Pi and mixed-harness scenarios are future evidence, not claims
already met. The shipped PM replay guide confirms the 50-record frozen
fixture; scoring and baseline observations must not be changed to favor Pi.
The later evaluation sample is not covered by the five-call spike allowance.

For each production slice, the required command correctly isolates a fresh
plugin-free server and its clients in one subshell:

```bash
(
  source scripts/test-herdr.sh
  corral_test_herdr_start || exit 1
  scripts/gate.sh
)
```

Probe/extension typechecks, tests and installation checks must name the exact
commands once the spike selects the runtime. Omitting a speculative package
command now is appropriate; production validation cannot remain unspecified
in the successor plan.

No code gate, build, implementation test, Pi process, live herdr experiment,

slices produce their evidence.

Owner decisions remain; owner acceptance must record each as `Resolved: <decision> => <resolution>`.

# T-102 P1 delegated owner decisions

The owner instructed: "Handling all of these automonously. not need to ask me for everything!"
These bounded decisions apply that explicit delegation to the current T-102 proposal.
The earlier owner request to approve T102 and the explicit subscription-only selection remain recorded.
This is an owner-decision receipt, not a fabricated independent technical verdict.
PR1 escalated only the unresolved owner decisions and found no blocking technical defect in the spike-only proposal.

Resolved: Approve or reject PM-first, extension-first, no-fork exploration while preserving current defaults and leaving native workers out of scope. => Approve the bounded PM-first, extension-first, no-fork compatibility exploration. Preserve current defaults and exclude native workers. Reconcile the T-109 product-direction report before any rollout; this does not select a new product default.

Resolved: Select the exact supported provider, authentication and model route for the spike, its spending cap, credential provisioning boundary and probe allowance; no existing subscription access is presumed transferable. => Target the existing OpenAI subscription through officially supported native sign-in only. The spike must discover and pin exact supported Pi/runtime/model versions before any live probe and must stop if documented support or native authentication is unavailable; no entitlement or credential compatibility is presumed. Permit at most five short compatibility calls with at most 1024 output tokens each and zero API spending. No paid API fallback or credential copying. Authentication and credentials remain in an isolated owner-controlled fixture, never in repository artifacts; actual interactive sign-in is required only if supported existing access is unavailable.

Resolved: Approve staged authorization in which initial acceptance permits only the bounded compatibility spike, and a successor reviewed plan is required before any production PM integration. => Approve spike-only staged authorization. Normal separate task/scope establishment remains required because accepting the single-scope P1 does not rewrite the proposal-only parent specification. Production integration and rollout require a successor independently reviewed plan and its normal acceptance. Durable mutation receipts and trusted exact-action binding must precede any future mutation-capable slice.

No gate, reviewer finding, identity check, or future recovery confirmation is waived.
